requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`.

**Obligations**
1. **Stop retrying when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first consecutive transient failure, including when `Retry-After` would pass that point.**
   - `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff]/fn[retry]` carries this out.
   - It records the time of the first consecutive failure in `failing`.
   - It stops when `now + delay > first + RETRY_LIMIT`. `RETRY_LIMIT` (`src/authoring/providers.rs#const[RETRY_LIMIT]`) is 60 seconds.
   - `delay` comes from `next_delay`, which returns the larger of the jittered delay and the `Retry-After` minimum. A `Retry-After` past the limit therefore stops retrying.
   - A non-transient error makes `next_delay` return `None`, so `retry` stops with that error unchanged.
   - `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` calls `backoff.retry` on each failure and returns the error on `Retry::Stop`. It resets the backoff only after a success.
2. **Fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts.**
   - `retry` builds "the provider kept failing for a minute after {attempts} attempts; …".
   - `converse` returns that error, which fails the assessment.
3. **Name the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.**
   - `retry` uses `failure_codes` and formats `HTTP {status} {code}`, `HTTP {status}`, or the bare code.
   - If neither is available, it falls back to the error text, for example for the ten-minute timeout.

**Tests**
- `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute]` carries a `{test}` reference and covers the following:
  - It checks that no attempt starts after the minute and that more than three attempts are made.
  - It checks the attempt count in the message and the "HTTP 429 ThrottlingException" text.
  - It checks that a `Retry-After` of 90 seconds stops at once.
  - It covers the status-only, code-only and timeout variants of the last-failure text.
  - It checks that a permanent failure stops with its own error.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_request_failing_for_a_minute_fails_the_assessment]` carries a `{test}` reference and runs end to end through `assess` and `converse` with a paused clock:
  - It asserts that the elapsed time is at most `RETRY_LIMIT` and that more than three attempts were made.
  - It asserts the error text "after {attempts} attempts; last failure: HTTP 503 ServiceUnavailableException".
  - It asserts that the final logged request is marked as not retried.

**Unspecified behavior**
- The fallback to the error text is within "when available".
- I found no other unspecified observable behavior in the `{impl}` code.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
